item.title: EKS Networking Refresher, Part 2: Pod Networking with the VPC CNI
item.description:
EKS Networking Refresher, Part 2: Pod Networking with the VPC CNI Link to heading

Part 1 covered how traffic gets into an EKS cluster. This part is about the other half: how pods get their IP addresses, and what happens when those addresses start running out. It covers the secondary IP range, custom networking, ENIConfig, security groups and SNAT.

Why Pod IPs Are a Problem on EKS Link to heading

In Part 1 we saw that an ALB in target-type: ip mode registers pod IPs as targets and talks to pods directly. That only works because the AWS VPC CNI gives every pod a real VPC IP, taken as a secondary address on an ENI.

item.title: EKS Networking Refresher, Part 1: Ingress and Load Balancers
item.description:
EKS Networking Refresher, Part 1: Ingress and Load Balancers Link to heading

If you last worked on EKS a few years ago, the picture in your head is probably “a LoadBalancer Service in front of an nginx ingress controller”. That still works, but most of it has moved on. Ingress is frozen, the most popular ingress controller has been retired, and load balancers can talk to pods directly.
